gates.title: Do lab-grown islet cells work as a treatment in people?
gates.plain: Yes, once they survive. In Vertex’s trial, all 12 people given the full dose reached their blood-sugar targets, and 10 of the 12 no longer needed insulin injections after a year. The catch is that they all take anti-rejection drugs, which is the problem Islet-1 is designed to remove.
gates.evidence: Vertex VX-880 (zimislecel). Reichman and colleagues, New England Journal of Medicine, 2025.

gates.title: Does the genetic cloak stop rejection without anti-rejection drugs?
gates.plain: It has worked once. In one person, donor islet cells edited to hide from the immune system were left alone for more than a year, with no anti-rejection drugs. That was a small safety study with a different set of edits, so it shows the idea can work, not that Islet-1’s cloak will.
gates.evidence: Sana UP421. Carlsson and colleagues, New England Journal of Medicine, 2025, with longer follow-up reported since.
gates.next: Next: show it holds for stem-cell islets with Islet-1’s edits (Stage 1, lab testing).

gates.title: Can the cells survive the autoimmune attack that caused the diabetes?
gates.plain: This is the hardest question, and it is only partly answered. People with type 1 diabetes already carry immune cells that remember how to attack beta cells. The one person given edited donor cells (hurdle 2) has type 1 diabetes, and the cells were left alone for more than a year, which is encouraging, but it was a small graft in a muscle, not a treatment. Design A adds a shield that switches on only when inflammation appears. Designs B and X keep that shield and change other parts of the design.
gates.evidence: The one human result so far (Sana UP421, above) used donor islets in a small dose. Nothing yet shows this for stem-cell islets at treatment size.
gates.next: Next: the first lab tests (Stage 1, lab testing).

gates.title: Does the oxygen layer keep the graft alive until blood vessels grow in?
gates.plain: A new graft has no blood vessels at first, so the design brings its own oxygen: a layer that releases it for the first three days while pre-built vessels link up. The blueprint’s computer model of the first 14 days suggests this can work, but with only a thin margin if our assumptions are pessimistic.
gates.evidence: From the blueprint’s own tissue model. None of its oxygen values has been measured in the lab.
gates.next: Next: blood supply and oxygen tests (Stage 2).
